title: Compact exterior-product arrows
statement: Let $C$ be a Grothendieck abelian symmetric monoidal closed coefficient category with sheafification, functorial flat resolutions and flat-preserving etale pullbacks, with the usual small-site sizes. For schemes over $B$, maps $f:X\to B$, $g:Y\to B$, and proper compactifications $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}\bar X\xrightarrow{p}B)$, $d=(Y\xrightarrow{j}\bar Y\xrightarrow{q}B)$, use [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and the derived exterior products of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]. Define $R\Gamma_c^c=R\Gamma(\bar X,i_!(-))$. The product compactification has middle scheme $\bar X\times_B\bar Y$ and the literal product open immersion. Exact inverse-image composition and tensor comparisons, followed by the inverse open-adjunction units, give the canonical restriction isomorphism $j_{XY}^*(i_!K\boxtimes j_!L)\cong K\boxtimes L$. Define $e:j_{XY,!}(K\boxtimes L)\to i_!K\boxtimes j_!L$ as its inverse's adjoint; it is an isomorphism, as is checked on geometric stalks. Define the compact exterior-product arrow $\kappa_c$ as the ordinary global exterior-product arrow on $i_!K,j_!L$, followed by $R\Gamma(e^{-1})$. Define the map on exterior products induced by morphisms $K\to K'$, $L\to L'$ by the derived tensor bifunctor on the two pulled-back morphisms. The generic bifunctor isomorphism of [lem-pur-support-site-comparison] assembles the two tensor-factor isomorphisms. For the compact arrow its product constant-sheaf functor is monoidal and preserves flat objects, as it does for coefficient modules. The restriction and compact exterior families are carried together with equations equating every component to the explicit composites just specified. Their normalized data are nonempty and determine their map components uniquely; choose the map component from this normalized data, retaining the normalization proof.

proof.text: For an open immersion j and arbitrary coefficients C as in the statement, prove the open projection map j_!(K tensor^L Lj^*M) to j_!K tensor^L M invertible. After exact restriction to j it is invertible by the adjunction unit and the inverse-image tensor comparison. After restriction to the closed complement both its source and target are zero, since the extension by zero vanishes there and a tensor with a zero factor is zero. Apply abstract derived open-closed conservativity. This is the proved private helper compactProductProjection_isIso; it generalizes the existing upstream projection-formula proof without adding coefficient assumptions.

Factor the product open J into two open immersions Jprime and J1. Let V be the pullback of c.i along the first compactified projection, with J1 its second projection; the map Jprime from X times_B Y to V is induced by the first projection and J. Pullback pasting identifies its square with d.i as cartesian, so it too is open. Base change identifies each pulled-back zero extension with an extension by zero. Apply the first projection formula, then the second in the opposite tensor order using symmetry, and compose the zero extensions. This gives an actual isomorphism from the exterior product of c.i_!K and d.i_!L to J_!(K exterior L). The generic tensor argument is the proved private helper compactProductTensorIso.

The preceding isomorphism places the exterior product of the two zero extensions in the essential image of J_!. The invertible unit makes J_! fully faithful, hence the counit at this object is an isomorphism (Mathlib Adjunction.isIso_counit_app_of_iso). By the counit formula for the adjunction hom equivalence, the specified compactProductExtension is J_! applied to the inverse restriction isomorphism, followed by that counit. Both factors are invertible, proving compactProductExtension_isIso for the original specified map.

Keep all constructions unchanged: the compactification uses the literal product scheme and open map; the restriction is the displayed pullback-tensor composite; the compact arrow is the ordinary exterior arrow followed by sections of the inverse comparison. The existing normalized-family existence proofs assemble their components directly.
